state.idea: Plan a lightweight drift check that reports when a live n8n workflow no longer matches its committed export in this repository. It must run as a separate operational workflow on a schedule, not inside the planning workflow. Output is a single human-readable report; it must not write to a database, must not modify any workflow, and must not require any new infrastructure. Define the exact comparison performed, what counts as drift, where the report is delivered, and one observable manual acceptance check. Treat this as planning only.

architect.summary: Introduce one new independent n8n operational workflow that runs on a schedule to detect configuration drift between live n8n workflows and their committed exports in this repository. It reuses existing n8n event invocation and data retrieval methods without modifying any workflows or requiring new infrastructure. The comparison is a normalized JSON diff ignoring non-significant metadata, considering any structural or configuration changes as drift. The resulting human-readable drift report is sent via the existing Nuxt UI's notification or logging facilities. Manual acceptance is done by verifying the generated report matches known workflow changes with no false positives. This avoids expanding the current system beyond owned components or persisting data externally, fitting the incremental evolution policy.
details: CURRENT: Existing components include the n8n workflow automation platform (implicitly owned) and the Nuxt UI (component 'nuxt') which handles user interactions and submissions. The current system handles idea validation and synchronous result rendering via API calls but does not perform ongoing drift detection. Evidence comes from the architecture snapshot describing Nuxt's API and n8n interactions without drift checking.

REUSE: Ownership of the n8n platform and Nuxt UI ('nuxt') is established; the new drift-check workflow operates within this scope. It reuses existing infrastructure (n8n credentials, secure API endpoints) and shares data retrieval capabilities. No new infrastructure or persistent databases are introduced, conforming to reuse of current capabilities and avoiding overlapping with 'agent-team' or 'contract' components.

CHANGE: Add a single new dedicated n8n workflow that runs on a fixed schedule (e.g., daily). This workflow fetches current live workflow JSON exports and compares them programmatically with the committed exports in the repository (retrieved read-only). Comparison ignores benign metadata (timestamps, IDs) and flags any structural or configuration discrepancies as drift. It creates a plain-text, human-readable report summarizing differences, delivered to the Nuxt UI notification/log system or an existing Slack/email channel linked from the current system. No workflow modifications or database writes occur.

DECISION: No changes to the existing planning or agent execution workflows. The drift-check is strictly operational and isolated to minimize risk. Report delivery integration reuses existing notification endpoints without adding new communication channels or persistence. The report format and comparison criteria are precisely defined to avoid scope creep.

ASSUMPTIONS: The repository exports for live workflows are accessible read-only during the drift check. The n8n platform permits scheduled workflows with credentials to fetch workflow definitions. Nuxt UI or an existing receiver can surface plain-text reports. The comparison logic can ignore non-configuration fields reliably without deep schema changes. No new approvals or credential expansions are needed.

BOUNDARY: The drift check excludes automatic remediation, detailed historical trend analysis, or multi-tenant separation. It does not persist data beyond transient report generation. Infrastructure and components outside existing n8n, Nuxt UI, and repository exports remain untouched. Acceptance testing covers only correctness and false-positive absence of the drift report, not broader integration.

details: PURPOSE: To detect and report drift when live n8n workflows differ from their committed JSON exports, enabling maintainers to identify unintended changes early without modifying workflows or adding new infrastructure.

IN SCOPE: Develop a single new scheduled n8n operational workflow that fetches live workflow JSON and compares it to repository exports; define exact comparison logic normalized by ignoring timestamps, IDs, and volatile metadata; produce a human-readable drift report; deliver report via existing Nuxt UI notification/logging endpoints; no persistence or workflow modification.

OUT OF SCOPE: Automatic remediation or rollback, storing reports in databases or files, adding new communication channels (email, Slack), multi-tenant isolation enhancements, integration with agent-team or contract components beyond defined reuse.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) The scheduled workflow triggers and completes without errors on the defined schedule. (2) Drift detection logic reliably ignores transient metadata and flags only true configuration differences. (3) Generated report accurately reflects known workflow changes (manual verified) with no false positives. (4) Report is delivered visibly in the Nuxt UI notification/log system using existing mechanisms. (5) No changes occur to workflows or persistent storage during execution.

OPEN QUESTIONS (BLOCKERS): Confirm reliable read-only access to repository workflow exports during scheduled runs; validate n8n credentials suffice to fetch live workflow definitions; verify Nuxt UI notification endpoints accept plain text or formatted messages for drift report display. ASSUMPTIONS: Repository exports are accessible read-only; n8n supports scheduled workflows using existing credentials; report delivery uses current Nuxt UI channels without new infrastructure; drift defined as any structural/configuration difference excluding known non-significant metadata is acceptable.

ARCHITECTURE LIMITS: Current snapshot shows no persistent storage for such reports and no tenant isolation; thus, this iteration avoids persistent state and multi-tenancy complexities. The drift workflow must not extend the agent-team or contract components except via defined reuse. The Nuxt component's 120-second default wait per response constrains workflow execution time, implying drift report generation must be efficient and synchronous notifications must fit within existing latencies.

developer.summary: Propose implementing a separate, scheduled n8n workflow that detects configuration drift by comparing live n8n workflow JSON exports against their committed repository copies. Drift is defined as any structural or configuration difference after normalizing and excluding non-significant metadata (e.g., timestamps, IDs). The resulting human-readable plain-text drift report is sent via existing Nuxt UI notification or logging endpoints without modifying workflows or writing to any database. Manual acceptance includes verifying that the report accurately flags known changes and reports no false positives. The plan respects current component ownership, avoids new infrastructure, and fits within existing architecture limits.
details: TOUCHPOINTS: (1) New n8n operational workflow named 'workflow-drift-check' triggered on a fixed schedule (e.g., daily). (2) Uses existing repository read-only access to fetch committed workflow JSON exports (likely via secure HTTP or git mirror endpoint). (3) Uses n8n API or credentials to fetch live workflow JSON exports. (4) Nuxt UI notification/log endpoints (component 'nuxt') for delivering plain-text drift reports. No modifications to 'agent-team' or 'contract' components.

STEPS: 1) Create 'workflow-drift-check' n8n workflow with a scheduler trigger node. 2) Retrieve committed workflow JSON exports from repository snapshot or accessible read-only source. 3) Retrieve current live workflow JSON exports from n8n. 4) Normalize both JSON sets by stripping volatile metadata fields (timestamps, unique IDs, last execution data). 5) Perform a deep comparison to detect differences in structure or configuration. 6) Generate a concise, human-readable plain-text report summarizing detected drifts per workflow. 7) Use Nuxt UI notification/log endpoint to deliver the report; validate content format. 8) Configure workflow to produce no side effects beyond reporting; no database writes or workflow modifications.

CONTRACT: The existing Nuxt webhook and notification APIs remain compatible. No changes occur to the planning workflow or agent-team webhook. The new workflow outputs a single plain-text drift report per run. Drift is defined solely as configuration or structural JSON differences after normalization. The live workflows themselves are not modified, preserving system integrity and existing API contracts. No data is persisted beyond transient report generation and notification delivery.

VALIDATION: Run the scheduled 'workflow-drift-check' manually on a test environment containing known differences to verify that reported drifts match intentional changes and no false positives occur. Confirm report appears correctly in Nuxt UI notifications or logs. Check logs to ensure no database writes or unexpected side effects. Review timing constraints to fit within Nuxt 120s wait. Validate normalization logic excludes transient metadata correctly.

ROLLBACK: If issues arise, disable the scheduled 'workflow-drift-check' workflow without deleting it, preserving audit and configuration. No persistent state is created, so no data rollback is needed. Existing workflows and repository exports remain unchanged, ensuring stable system behavior.

DOCUMENTATION: Update repository architecture docs to include the new operational workflow 'workflow-drift-check' with description of comparison criteria, normalization rules (ignored fields), schedule, report format, and delivery mechanism. Document manual acceptance criteria and operational instructions (e.g., how to disable the workflow). Note assumptions about read-only repository export access and Nuxt notification capabilities to guide future review.
